s0201.literal: Xin Chao and Peng Min—the crown and cap of Qin and Long;
s0201.idiomatic: Xin Chao and Peng Min stand foremost among the gentry of Qin and Longyou.

s0202.literal: Fei Min and Ma Fu—leading clans of the central provinces;
s0202.idiomatic: Fei Min and Ma Fu head eminent families of the heartland.

s0203.literal: Zhang Chang—a scion of the old Liang royal house;
s0203.idiomatic: Zhang Chang carries the blood of the former Liang kings.

s0204.literal: Zhang Mu, Bian Xian, Wen Qi, Yang Ban, Liang Song, and Zhao Chang—in martial valor they match Flying and Feathered.
s0204.idiomatic: Zhang Mu, Bian Xian, Wen Qi, Yang Ban, Liang Song, and Zhao Chang fight with the renown of Li Guang and Huo Qubing.

s0205.literal: With Your Highness's divine strategy, governing them with prestige and faith, cultivating both agriculture and war, setting up both civil and military teaching—you could league and counter-league across the empire; how could the lands west of the River alone suffice as your limit!
s0205.idiomatic: Under your genius, rule them with awe and good faith; train the fields and the ranks alike, and pair arms with letters—you could play the great powers against one another under heaven. Why should the Hexi corridor be the end of your ambition?

s0206.literal: Rutan was greatly pleased and granted Zong Chang twenty horses.
s0206.idiomatic: Rutan was delighted and gave Zong Chang twenty horses.

s0207.literal: Thereupon he held a great feast for civil and military officials in the Hall of Modest Radiance, distributing gifts of gold and horses in varying measure.
s0207.idiomatic: He then feasted his civil and military officers in the Hall of Modest Radiance, awarding gold and horses in graded shares.

s0208.literal: He sent Western Bureau Attendant Shi Hao as envoy to pay a courtesy visit to Yao Xing.
s0208.idiomatic: He dispatched Shi Hao of the Western Bureau as envoy to Yao Xing.

s0209.literal: Xing said to Hao: "The General of Chariots and Cavalry has settled Liangzhou and returned in brocade to his native state—does he owe me gratitude?"
s0209.idiomatic: Yao Xing asked Hao, "The Chariots-and-Cavalry General has secured Liangzhou and come home in glory—does he feel beholden to me?"

s0210.literal: Hao replied: "The General amassed merit west of the He, but little spread his fine renown; Your Majesty's royal majesty had not yet reached him, and he pledged loyalty from ten thousand li away. Your Majesty appoints talent to office and grants posts according to merit—the constant norms of order; what debt of gratitude is there!"
s0210.idiomatic: Hao answered, "The General built his name in Hexi and offered allegiance from afar before your majesty's writ had reached him. You place men by merit and office by measure—that is the way of kings. What debt is there?"

s0211.literal: Xing said: "Had I not granted the province to the General, how would he have obtained it?"
s0211.idiomatic: Xing said, "If I had not given him the province, how would he have gained it?"

s0212.literal: Hao said: "That Hexi was clouded with turmoil and the Lü house overthrown—this was truly because the General and his brothers overturned their foundation."
s0212.idiomatic: Hao said, "The storms in Hexi and the fall of the Lü were wrought by the General and his brothers uprooting their rule."

s0213.literal: Your Majesty though your great net spreads to distant lands, Liangzhou remained outside Heaven's mesh.
s0213.idiomatic: Though your reach extends far, Liangzhou still lay beyond your net.

s0214.literal: Hence the Campaigning West General, with the weight of the Zhou dukes of Zhou and Shao, had his strength broken at Guzang;
s0214.idiomatic: So the Campaigning West General, burdened like the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, was spent before Guzang;

s0215.literal: Qi Nan with the splendor of the royal host had his momentum checked at Zhangye.
s0215.idiomatic: and Qi Nan, at the head of the imperial host, was turned back at Zhangye.

s0216.literal: Wang Shang held a lone city in isolation, pressed from without by hordes of barbarians; unless Your Majesty campaigned in force for ten years and exhausted the Middle Kingdom, Liangzhou would not be easily taken.
s0216.idiomatic: Wang Shang held one city alone against surrounding tribes. Without ten years of war and the draining of the realm, Liangzhou would not have been easily won.

s0217.literal: Now by lending an empty title you gain within a great profit—thus one knows subtle calculation comes from Heaven and the Sage accords with the Way; though it is called a transfer of appointment, it is surely timely.
s0217.idiomatic: Now you grant a hollow title and reap a rich gain within—proof that Heaven aids your reckoning and the sage-king moves with the Way. Though men call it a transfer of office, it is simply what the hour demands.

s0218.literal: Xing was pleased with his words and appointed him Cavalry Commandant.
s0218.idiomatic: Pleased with his reply, Xing made him Cavalry Commandant.

s0219.literal: Rutan feasted his officials in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and, looking up, sighed: "The ancients said 'he who builds does not dwell in it; he who dwells in it does not build'—how true!"
s0219.idiomatic: Rutan entertained his ministers in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue, gazed upward, and sighed, "The ancients were right: those who build do not long enjoy; those who enjoy did not build."

s0220.literal: Meng Yi advanced and said: "Prince Zhang Wen of Former Liang built walls and parks and repaired ancestral temples as resources to pass down and an enterprise for ten thousand generations—yet when Qin troops crossed the river, it dissolved streaming away."
s0220.idiomatic: Meng Yi spoke up: "Prince Zhang Wen raised walls and gardens and restored the ancestral shrines for heirs yet unborn—yet when Qin armies crossed the river, his house melted away like ice in sun."

s0221.literal: Liang Xi held the territory of the whole province and commanded a host of a hundred thousand; his army was defeated at Jiuquan and he himself died at Pengji.
s0221.idiomatic: Liang Xi held the whole province and a hundred thousand men, yet lost his army at Jiuquan and his life at Pengji.

s0222.literal: The Lü house with momentum to topple mountains ruled the Western Xia, yet the realm collapsed and they came bearing jade to Qin and Yong.
s0222.idiomatic: The Lü, who seemed able to overturn mountains and ruled Western Xia, saw their lands crumble until they surrendered with jade seals to Qin and Yong.

s0223.literal: Kuang Rao had a saying: 'Wealth and rank have no constancy; suddenly they pass to another.'
s0223.idiomatic: Kuang Rao once said, "Fortune and office never stay fixed; in a blink they change hands."

s0224.literal: This hall has stood nearly a hundred years and known twelve lords; only trust and obedience can long preserve, and benevolence and righteousness can eternally secure—may Your Highness exert yourself therein.
s0224.idiomatic: This hall is nearly a century old and has seen twelve masters. Only loyalty and compliance keep a house long; only benevolence and right keep it firm. I urge Your Highness to live by that.

s0225.literal: Rutan said: "Without you I would not have heard such upright counsel."
s0225.idiomatic: Rutan said, "Without you I would never have heard such honest counsel."

s0226.literal: Though Rutan was subject to Yao Xing, his chariots, robes, and ritual regalia were entirely like a king's.
s0226.idiomatic: Though he owed allegiance to Yao Xing, Rutan's carriages, dress, and court ritual matched a king's.

s0227.literal: He appointed Zong Chang Registrar of the Grand Treasury and Recorder of Secretariat affairs.
s0227.idiomatic: He made Zong Chang Registrar of the Grand Treasury and chief recorder of the secretariat.

s0228.literal: Rutan feigned a tour of the Jiao River and surreptitiously moved more than thirty thousand households of the various Qiang of Xiping and Huangshui to the four commanderies of Wuxing, Fanhe, Wuwei, and Changsong.
s0228.idiomatic: Pretending a pleasure tour along the Jiao River, Rutan secretly relocated more than thirty thousand Qiang households from Xiping and Huangshui into Wuxing, Fanhe, Wuwei, and Changsong.

s0229.literal: He mustered more than fifty thousand troops of both barbarian and Chinese arms, held a grand review at Fangting, and then marched against Juqu Mengxun, entering Western Shaan.
s0229.idiomatic: He gathered over fifty thousand barbarian and Chinese troops, reviewed them at Fangting, and marched against Juqu Mengxun into western Shaan.

s0230.literal: Mengxun led his forces to oppose him; they fought at Junshi and Rutan was defeated by Mengxun.
s0230.idiomatic: Mengxun came out to meet him; at Junshi Rutan was beaten.

s0231.literal: Rutan led twenty thousand horse and transported forty thousand piculs of grain to supply Western Commandery.
s0231.idiomatic: Rutan led twenty thousand cavalry and hauled forty thousand piculs of grain to provision Western Commandery.

s0232.literal: Mengxun attacked Western Commandery and took it.
s0232.idiomatic: Mengxun assaulted Western Commandery and captured it.

s0233.literal: Afterward Rutan again fought Helian Bobo at Yangwu and was beaten by Bobo; more than ten of his officers and aides died. Rutan fled south into the mountains with a few horse and was nearly caught by pursuing riders.
s0233.idiomatic: Later Rutan fought Helian Bobo at Yangwu and lost again; a dozen officers fell. He escaped into the southern hills with only a few riders and was almost overtaken.

s0234.literal: Rutan, fearing enemies from east and west, moved the populace within three hundred li into Guzang; the realm was stricken with alarm and resentment.
s0234.idiomatic: Fearing attack from both quarters, Rutan moved everyone within three hundred li into Guzang, and the whole state groaned in fear and anger.

s0235.literal: The Tufa Cheng Qi'er, taking advantage of the people's distress, led three hundred of his followers in rebellion against Rutan at the North City.
s0235.idiomatic: Cheng Qi'er of the Tufa, exploiting the people's turmoil, led three hundred men in revolt at the North City.

s0236.literal: They tried to make Liang Gui covenant chief, but Gui shut his door and would not respond.
s0236.idiomatic: They pressed Liang Gui to lead them, but he barred his gate and refused.

s0237.literal: In one night the mob grew to several thousand.
s0237.idiomatic: By morning their numbers had swelled to several thousand.

s0238.literal: Palace Interior Commandant Zhang Meng addressed the crowd loudly: "Our lord's defeat at Yangwu was surely because he relied on numbers."
s0238.idiomatic: Palace Commandant Zhang Meng cried to the throng, "Our lord's loss at Yangwu came of trusting too many men."

s0239.literal: To blame oneself and repent is the duty of an enlightened ruler—why do you gentlemen follow this petty man in an unrighteous deed!
s0239.idiomatic: A wise ruler blames himself and mends his ways—why follow this nobody into treason?

s0240.literal: The palace guard is even now closing in; the peril before your eyes—regret will come too late.
s0240.idiomatic: The palace guard is already on you. Disaster is at hand; repent now or never.

s0241.literal: When the crowd heard this, all dispersed.
s0241.idiomatic: At his words the mob melted away.

s0242.literal: Qi'er fled to Yanran; Palace Cavalry General Bai Lu and others pursued and beheaded him.
s0242.idiomatic: Qi'er fled to Yanran; Bai Lu, palace cavalry commander, overtook and killed him.

s0243.literal: Military Adviser Sacrificial Officer Liang Pou, Assisting State Major Bian Xian, and seven others plotted rebellion; Rutan executed them all.
s0243.idiomatic: Liang Pou, military adviser, Bian Xian, assisting-state major, and five others plotted revolt; Rutan put them all to death.

s0244.literal: Yao Xing, because Rutan had without the Yangwu defeat and within the Bian and Liang troubles, sent his Master of Writing Wei Zong to observe whether there was an opening.
s0244.idiomatic: With Yangwu lost without and the Bian and Liang plots within, Yao Xing sent Master of Writing Wei Zong to probe for weakness.

s0245.literal: Rutan debated with Zong the schemes of the Six States' alliances and the strategies of the Three Kingdoms' wars, speaking from afar on the rise and fall ordained by Heaven and from near on success and failure in human affairs—infinite in resource, his rhetoric lucid and keen.
s0245.idiomatic: Rutan discoursed with him on Warring States alliances and Three Kingdoms stratagems, on Heaven's mandate in the distance and men's fortunes close at hand—endlessly inventive, his speech bright and sharp.

s0246.literal: Zong left and sighed: "A generation-defining great talent who orders civilization through the classics need not be from a splendid clan or Xia gentry;"
s0246.idiomatic: Leaving, Zong sighed, "A man who shapes an age and orders the rites need not spring from a noble house or Han stock;"

s0247.literal: one who clears troubles, settles chaos, clarifies the spirit, and aids the age need not have studied the Eight Canons or Nine Mounds.
s0247.idiomatic: nor need one who cuts through disorder and steadies the realm have read the Eight Canons or Nine Mounds.

s0248.literal: Beyond the Five Classics, atop the crown of excellence, there are again men of their own kind.
s0248.idiomatic: Outside the Five Classics, among the foremost of the land, others still arise.

s0249.literal: The General is divine in counsel and splendid in gifts—truly a great man of an age; You Yu and Lil Wenzhen are hardly worth counting!
s0249.idiomatic: The Chariots-and-Cavalry General is keen-witted and brilliant—a true giant of his time. You Yu and Jinti are nothing beside him!

s0250.literal: Zong returned to Chang'an and said to Xing: "Though Liangzhou is in the aftermath of ruin, its customs have not yet collapsed. Rutan is resourceful in many stratagems and leans on the strength of mountains and rivers—it cannot yet be plotted against."
s0250.idiomatic: Back in Chang'an, Zong told Xing, "Liangzhou is battered but not broken. Rutan is cunning and holds the mountains and rivers—do not think him easy prey."

s0251.literal: Xing said: "Bobo with a mob still broke him—how could he stand against me with the armies of the empire!"
s0251.idiomatic: Xing said, "Bobo with a rabble beat him. With the armies of the realm, how can I fail?"

s0252.literal: Zong said: "Forms shift and momentum changes; beginning and end follow different paths. He who bullies others is easily defeated; he who holds himself is hard to assault."
s0252.idiomatic: Zong said, "Situations turn; what worked once fails next. The aggressor breaks easily; the defender is hard to crack."

s0253.literal: At Yangwu Rutan underestimated Bobo and met defeat.
s0253.idiomatic: At Yangwu Rutan slighted Bobo and lost.

s0254.literal: Now with a great army bearing down, he will surely fortify himself and seek preservation; I privately judge none of his ministers can match Rutan.
s0254.idiomatic: If a great host comes now, he will dig in and save himself—and I doubt any of his ministers equal Rutan.

s0255.literal: Even with Heaven's majesty pressing upon him, I see no profit in it.
s0255.idiomatic: Even with imperial might against him, I see little gain.

s0256.literal: Xing would not heed him and sent his generals Yao Bi and Qincheng at the head of thirty thousand foot and horse to attack, also sending his general Yao Xian to follow Bi as rear guard. He sent Rutan a letter saying: "I have dispatched Minister of the Left Qi Nan to punish Bobo, fearing he might flee west—therefore I have Bi and others intercept him in Hexi."
s0256.idiomatic: Xing refused and sent Yao Bi and Qincheng with thirty thousand foot and horse to invade, with Yao Xian following as reserve. He wrote Rutan: "I have sent Qi Nan, Minister of the Left, against Bobo and fear he may slip west—Bi is posted in Hexi to block him."

s0257.literal: Rutan believed it and therefore made no preparations.
s0257.idiomatic: Rutan took the letter at face value and left his guard down.

s0258.literal: Bi's host reached Mokou; Changsong Administrator Su Ba barred the gates and held firm. Bi urged Ba to surrender. Ba said: "You have broken your sworn oath and attack a submissive frontier state—Heaven and Earth have spirit; they will not bless you!"
s0258.idiomatic: Bi reached Mokou; Su Ba, Changsong's governor, shut the walls. Bi called on him to yield. Ba replied, "You broke your oath and strike a loyal frontier—Heaven and Earth see; they will not aid you!"

s0259.literal: I would rather be a Liang ghost—why should I surrender!
s0259.idiomatic: I would sooner be a ghost of Liang than submit—never!

s0260.literal: The city fell and Ba was beheaded.
s0260.idiomatic: The city fell; Su Ba was beheaded.

s0261.literal: Bi reached Guzang and encamped in the Western Park.
s0261.idiomatic: Bi came to Guzang and camped in the Western Park.

s0262.literal: Prefecture natives Wang Zhong, Song Zhong, Wang E, and others secretly served as inside collaborators; scouts seized their messenger and delivered him.
s0262.idiomatic: Wang Zhong, Song Zhong, Wang E, and others of the province plotted treason within; scouts caught their courier and brought him in.

s0263.literal: Rutan wished to execute the ringleaders; Vanguard General Yiliyanhou said: "Now with a strong foe outside and traitors within, armies clashing and momentum cramped—calamity is no light matter. All should be thrown into pits to secure within and without."
s0263.idiomatic: Rutan meant to kill the leaders; vanguard general Yiliyanhou said, "With the enemy outside and traitors inside, battle pressing and peril near, the danger is grave. Exterminate them all to steady within and without."

s0264.literal: Rutan followed this, killing more than five thousand, and took the women as military rewards.
s0264.idiomatic: Rutan agreed, slaughtered more than five thousand, and gave the women to the troops as booty.

s0265.literal: He ordered all commanderies and districts to drive cattle and sheep into the open country; Qincheng let his troops loose to plunder captives.
s0265.idiomatic: He ordered every district to drive herds into the open; Qincheng's men swept the countryside for plunder.

s0266.literal: Rutan sent his Pacifier of the North Juyan, Pacifier of the Army Jing Gui, and ten other generals with cavalry to strike in separate columns, routing them severely and taking more than seven thousand heads.
s0266.idiomatic: Rutan sent Juyan, Pacifier of the North, Jing Gui, Pacifier of the Army, and ten other generals with cavalry in separate strikes, crushing them and taking more than seven thousand heads.

s0267.literal: Yao Bi held his ramparts and would not come out; Rutan assaulted but could not take him and therefore dammed the river's upper reaches, intending to wear them down over time.
s0267.idiomatic: Yao Bi held his walls and would not fight; Rutan could not break him and cut the river upstream, planning to starve him out.

s0268.literal: Heavy rain came; the dam burst and Bi's army revived.
s0268.idiomatic: Torrential rain broke the dam; Bi's army rallied.

s0269.literal: Yao Xian heard Bi had been defeated and marched by forced stages to his aid; his army's momentum was very strong.
s0269.idiomatic: Hearing Bi had lost, Yao Xian rushed up by forced marches with overwhelming force.

s0270.literal: He sent archery officers Meng Qin and five others to challenge at Liangfeng Gate; before their bowstrings could be drawn, Weapons Officers General Song Yi and others galloped out and cut them down.
s0270.idiomatic: He sent archer Meng Qin and five others to duel at Liangfeng Gate; before they could loose, weapons officer Song Yi and others charged out and killed them.

s0271.literal: Xian then laid the blame on Qincheng.
s0271.idiomatic: Xian then blamed Qincheng for the defeat.

s0272.literal: He sent envoys to apologize to Rutan and withdrew his army.
s0272.idiomatic: He sent envoys to make peace with Rutan and pulled his troops back.

s0273.literal: Rutan thereupon presumed to ascend the throne of Liang, amnestied his domain, changed the era name to Jiaping, and established the full bureaucracy.
s0273.idiomatic: Rutan then took the title King of Liang, proclaimed an amnesty, adopted the era name Jiaping, and installed a full court.

s0274.literal: He made Lady Sheju queen among five consorts, heir Wu Tai crown prince and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Left Chief Recorder Zhao Chao and Right Chief Recorder Guo Xing Left and Right Masters of Writing, Juyan Grand Commandant, Jing Gui Colonel of the Masters of Convoy, and the rest received titles and posts in due measure.
s0274.idiomatic: He made Lady Sheju chief among five consorts, heir Wu Tai crown prince and overseer of the Masters of Writing, Zhao Chao and Guo Xing left and right masters, Juyan Grand Commandant, Jing Gui metropolitan colonel, and enfeoffed the rest in graded ranks.

s0275.literal: He sent Left General Kumu and Master of the Horse Hu Kang against Juqu Mengxun, carried off more than a thousand households from Lin-song, and returned.
s0275.idiomatic: He sent Left General Kumu and Horse-Master Hu Kang against Mengxun, seized more than a thousand households at Linsong, and withdrew.

s0276.literal: Mengxun was greatly angered, led five thousand horse to Fangting in Xianmei, crushed the Chegai Xianbei, and returned.
s0276.idiomatic: Mengxun, furious, led five thousand horse to Fangting in Xianmei, broke the Chegai Xianbei, and turned back.

s0277.literal: Juyan again campaigned against Mengxun and returned in great defeat.
s0277.idiomatic: Juyan attacked Mengxun again and came home routed.

s0278.literal: Rutan was about to lead the host in person against Mengxun; Zhao Chao and Grand Astrologer Jing Bao remonstrated: "Now Venus has not yet risen and Jupiter is in the west—one should hold to defense; it is hard to attack others."
s0278.idiomatic: Rutan prepared to lead the army against Mengxun in person; Zhao Chao and grand astrologer Jing Bao urged, "Venus has not yet risen and Jupiter stands in the west—defend, do not strike."

s0279.literal: In recent years the heavens have been in disorder and winds and mists untimely; only by cultivating virtue and blaming oneself can fortune be settled.
s0279.idiomatic: Heaven's signs have been errant these years, winds and mists out of season. Only virtue and self-reproach can restore fortune.

s0280.literal: Rutan said: "In years past Mengxun behaved shamelessly, entered our borders, raided our frontiers, and ruined our grain."
s0280.idiomatic: Rutan said, "Mengxun has long trampled our borders, looted our marches, and destroyed our crops."

s0281.literal: I have stored strength awaiting the hour to avenge the shame of the eastern gate; now the great army is gathered—do you wish to discourage the host?
s0281.idiomatic: I have waited to wipe away the shame of the eastern gate. The host is ready—will you damp their spirit?

s0282.literal: Bao said: "Your Majesty, not holding me unworthy, made me oversee the celestial signs; if I see how matters stand and do not speak, that is not the way of a minister."
s0282.idiomatic: Bao said, "Your Majesty set me to read the sky. If I see peril and stay silent, I fail my office."

s0283.literal: The astronomy is manifest clear—if we move, there can be no profit.
s0283.idiomatic: The stars are plain: march now and we cannot win.

s0284.literal: Rutan said: "I shall attack with fifty thousand light horse; if Mengxun meets me with cavalry alone, numbers will not match;"
s0284.idiomatic: Rutan said, "I take fifty thousand light horse. If Mengxun meets me with horse alone, he cannot match my numbers;"

s0285.literal: if he comes with mixed foot as well, swift and slow will not align;
s0285.idiomatic: if he mixes foot soldiers, fast and slow will not keep step;

s0286.literal: rescue the right and I strike the left, hurry forward and I attack the rear—I will never join him in pitched battle—what do you fear?
s0286.idiomatic: relieve his right and I hit his left; rush his van and I take his rear. I will never give him a stand-up fight—what is there to fear?

s0287.literal: Bao said: "Heaven's signs are not empty; change is sure to come."
s0287.idiomatic: Bao said, "Heaven does not lie. Disaster will come."

s0288.literal: Rutan in anger had Bao shackled and marched off, saying: "If you prove right I ought to kill you as an example; if wrong I will enfeoff you Marquis of a Hundred Households." Soon Mengxun led his forces to oppose him; they fought at Qiongquan and Rutan was routed, fleeing back on a single horse.
s0288.idiomatic: Rutan, furious, had Bao chained and marched, saying, "If you are right I will kill you before the army; if wrong I will make you marquis of a hundred households." Mengxun met him at Qiongquan; Rutan was shattered and fled home alone.

s0289.literal: Jing Bao was seized by Mengxun, who reproached him: "You are clear in astronomy and were employed by that state—yet you defied Heaven and violated the norm; where then was your wisdom?"
s0289.idiomatic: Mengxun captured Jing Bao and rebuked him: "You read the heavens for that court yet marched against Heaven's will—where was your wisdom?"

s0290.literal: Bao said: "It is not that I lacked wisdom, but that I spoke and was not heeded."
s0290.idiomatic: Bao said, "I was not without wisdom; my lord would not listen."

s0291.literal: Mengxun said: "In former days Han High Ancestor was besieged at Pingcheng and made Lou Jing's counsel his merit;"
s0291.idiomatic: Mengxun said, "When Gaozu of Han was trapped at Pingcheng, he honored Lou Jing's advice;"

s0292.literal: Yuan Shao was defeated at Guandu and Tian Feng was put to death.
s0292.idiomatic: when Yuan Shao lost at Guandu, he killed Tian Feng.

s0293.literal: Your stratagem matches those two; your noble lord's measure cannot yet be reckoned.
s0293.idiomatic: Your counsel matches theirs; your lord's mind cannot yet be read.

s0294.literal: Surely you deserve Lou Jing's reward; I release you now—only I fear you may meet Tian Feng's fate."
s0294.idiomatic: You may win Lou Jing's reward; I spare you now—but you may yet suffer Tian Feng's end."

s0295.literal: Bao said: "Though my lord is not the equal of Han High Ancestor, he is still unlike Yuan Shao at the start—I may simply fail to receive a fief; why should I fear execution?"
s0295.idiomatic: Bao said, "My lord is no Gaozu, but he is no Yuan Shao either. I may miss a fief; I do not fear the axe."

s0297.literal: Reaching Guzang, Rutan apologized to him: "You are my tortoise and yarrow, yet I could not follow you—my deep fault."
s0297.idiomatic: Back in Guzang, Rutan said to him, "You were my oracle, and I would not heed you—that is my grave fault."

s0298.literal: He enfeoffed him Marquis of Bao'anting.
s0298.idiomatic: He enfeoffed him as Marquis of Bao'anting.

s0299.literal: Mengxun advanced to invest Guzang; the people, remembering the slaughter at the Eastern Park, all fled in alarm.
s0299.idiomatic: Mengxun pressed on Guzang; remembering the massacre at the Eastern Park, the people scattered in terror.

s0300.literal: The Leiju, Maitian, Chegai, and other tribes all submitted to Mengxun.
s0300.idiomatic: The Leiju, Maitian, Chegai, and other tribal groups all surrendered to Mengxun.
